items.title: ChatGPT 新增“实时听写”功能：对着麦克风说话，语音能即时变文字
items.description: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，ChatGPT 今天宣布新增“实时听写”功能，用户对着麦克风说话时，语音就能同步转换成文字，不必等录音结束后再转写，让 ChatGPT 更快接收到语音指令 。 该功能将陆续向全球所有 ChatGPT 用户开放，覆盖网页版、桌面客户端及 iOS 和 Android 应用。使用时， 用户只需点击音频波形，就能查看实时转写的文字 ，录音结束后还可以直接在输入框中编辑。 OpenAI 还宣布，取消 ChatGPT 语音听写原有的 10 分钟时长限制，并进一步提高转写的可靠性。今年早些时候，ChatGPT 的双向语音对话模式曾迎来全面改版。 OpenAI 去年还推出了用于转写语音笔记和会议内容的“录制模式”，不过仍处于测试阶段，仅面向 Plus、Enterprise、Edu、Business 和 Pro 工作区开放。 据IT之家了解，用户也可以利用 ChatGPT 输入框的语音听写功能，让 ChatGPT 将语音消息转成文字，或整理成条列式要点。

items.content: 《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）首批媒体评测于 11 月 18 日公开。据《综艺》当天报道，游戏在 Metacritic 获得 99 分，追平 1998 年 N64 版《塞尔达传说：时之笛》的平台历史最高分。Rockstar 官网确认，游戏于 11 月 19 日登陆 PS5 和 Xbox Series X|S。 The Verge 的评测在接近 80 小时体验后，肯定了杰森与露西娅的双主角关系，以及与开放世界玩法结合的叙事。故事设定在以佛罗里达州为原型的 Leonida，玩家可分别扮演两人，并逐步建立他们的关系；除主线任务外，也可通过不同活动探索罪恶都市、海滩和沼泽等地区。 该评测使用首发版 PS5，称整体运行良好，但也提到战斗操作仍显笨重、武器轮盘容易误选，以及少量物理和道具显示错误。完成主线并游玩超过 70 小时后，评测者的总进度仍不足 60%。 谷歌 11 月 18 日发布 Gemini 4 Neon，面向软件开发、知识工作和科学研究，开始向 Gemini API、Gemini for business、Antigravity 及 Gemini 应用开放。其中，Gemini 应用和 Antigravity 面向 Google AI Pro、Ultra 订阅用户。 Neon 支持 100 万 Token 上下文，可综合处理电子表格、PDF、图表、音频和视频。API 每百万输入 Token 收费 3 美元、输出收费 15 美元，缓存输入为 0.15 美元。谷歌称，在默认 high 思考档位下，Neon 在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 保持较高能力的同时，单任务成本比 Carbon 低 32%。 模型可独立完成多步骤任务，也能在 Antigravity 中调度 Hydrogen 子智能体。按谷歌公布的测试，Neon 在 xhigh 档位的 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 得分为 61，位列第三；在默认 high 档位的 FrontierCode 2.0 测试中得分为 46.2%。

items.content: 所以判断一门影像手艺成没成，有个简单粗暴的试金石：敢不敢上大银幕。胶片当年闯过这关，数字摄影机也闯过，三维动画同样闯过，每闯过一关，就意味着一项新技术拿到了成熟影像工业的入场券。 过去两年，AI 视频生成你方唱罢我登场，一个比一个惊艳，可真正到了商业制作的修罗场，甲方要的是原生 4K，导演想一镜到底，品牌方动不动就改需求，制作团队还得在成本、周期和最终交付之间走钢丝。 最近，爱范儿注意到即梦 Seedance 2.5 推出了 4K 版本，把最长 30 秒单次生成、全模态参考、视频编辑与延长等本领一并拉到了更高的画质规格。 过去体验 AI 视频模型，我总习惯给它安排一些足够热闹的场面。巨型怪兽、千军万马、末日都市，最好再来点爆炸与运镜，十几秒的视频也能拍出大片预告的气势。 但仔细想想，真正让商业制作团队头疼的，可能是一瓶香水上的标签、一张在不同渠道反复使用的商品图，或者导演临时要求修改的某个镜头。 假设客户要拍一条高端机械腕表广告，镜头从表盘的极近距离开始，掠过钻石时标和日期窗口，最后缓缓后退，露出放在私人书房里的完整腕表。

items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: Productivity apps are simultaneously trying to feed more context to their AI tools while also making those AI assistants available in every nook and corner of their products. Superhuman (formerly Grammarly) is going in the same direction with the rollout of features, including a personalized Go assistant, making agents available in Docs, and third-party agent integrations. While some of the company’s AI features have faced criticism , Superhuman started pushing its Go assistant after its rebranding last year . With the new rollout, it is making Go learn context across different apps and give better personalized suggestions for prompts. Superhuman is revamping its onboarding flow to let users connect their preferred tools and load context about their work upfront. The assistant works inline with the cursor — just like Grammarly does — and also manages other agents. Superhuman is also making the agent proactive, which means it looks for your schedule, keeps an eye on your email, and even drafts responses. The updated Go agent also learns users’ writing styles and responds accordingly in email and Docs. The productivity company is adding 20 new connected agents, including DeepL, Legora, Amplitude, Databricks, and Blackboard, through its Go SDK. The company is also thinking about adding AI to different products, including Docs and Superhuman Mail. items.description: “I don’t think [Huang is] disloyal to the United States," Musk said.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk elaborated on his thoughts about Nvidia’s leadership change. “Jensen is an old friend of mine,” Musk said. “I would call Jensen, you know, Michael Jordan at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team.” On X, the social media platform he owns, Musk even said he would hire Huang. “He’s one of the most talented entrepreneur-CEOs in history,” Musk said when asked about his X post. “Who wouldn’t want to hire Jensen?” Musk also signed a petition , alongside over 200,000 other people, urging Nvidia to reinstate its former CEO. Nvidia’s board, however, confirmed it is not planning to bring Huang back. “[It] doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me…” Musk said of that decision. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.”

items.content: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella predicts that the rise of AI agents is going to reshape the economics of the internet, impacting the business models of the companies that rely on advertising and what he referred to as “human web” traffic. items.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range
items.description: The long-awaited IPO reportedly values the company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: Anthropic has priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share , above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry. The Claude maker sold 980 million shares in the offering, up from the 825 million initially planned, generating $81.3 billion in proceeds and surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion record to become the largest IPO in history by proceeds raised. At the IPO price, Anthropic is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market round , but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago. Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks. The company’s performance is expected to set expectations for private AI companies, including Anthropic’s main rival OpenAI, which was last reportedly valued at $1.25 billion but has yet to announce plans for an IPO. items.title: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report
items.description: One Wall Street analyst got to the bottom of Nvidia's surprise announcement that it wouldn't be filing its formal quarterly results document, the 10-Q, for weeks.
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: During Nvidia’s quarterly call on Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress dropped this little oddity: She said Nvidia wouldn’t be immediately filing its quarterly results report, known as a 10-Q, with the SEC. “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks.” And she offered no reason why. The delay was widely noticed. Among the many comments on X about it , economic and investment analyst Edward Dowd called it a “red flag.” Nvidia has typically filed the 10-Q the same day it reports results. The 10-Q offers far more detail about a company’s operations than an earnings press release, including sections that disclose “legal proceedings,” which include lawsuits that could affect the company; and “risk factors,” which cover other potentially business-impairing items. The announcement of the delay was so unusual that UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked about it after the public earnings call. Nvidia told him the delay was related to whether the company would need to disclose additional information about its ongoing investigation into Huang in the 10-Q. “The company announced that the 10-Q will be filed ‘in the coming weeks’ – later than usual. When queried on our callback, management indicated this was related to the ongoing investigation and whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing,” Arcuri wrote in his research note. items.title: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’
items.description: The Anduril co-founder says outdated technology is leaving systems vulnerable to a new wave of AI-enabled attacks.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, Palmer Luckey warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Addressing the recent spate of tech outages, the Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder argued that older systems are struggling to keep pace with the new hacking capabilities enabled by AI and warned it was time to quicken the pace of securing our defenses. “We’re seeing the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools allowing for the creation of various exploits,” he said. While government officials largely attributed the latest set of technical issues to companies rushing to patch their systems to protect against the new vulnerabilities AI has discovered, Luckey focused on the underlying security challenges facing organizations using outdated technology. Luckey explained that U.S. adversaries are currently exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and our defense capabilities. These attacks are being carried out for both strategic and financial reasons, and North Korea was particularly involved, he added. The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, noted that U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance had canceled his appearance at the Times’ conference this week because of the recent tech outages, saying he now had to attend meetings about the matter. Given the situation, Sorkin asked Luckey how worried we should be about all this.

items.author: Amanda Silberling

items.title: Sam Altman says his life is so weird that he’s unfazed by Andrew Garfield portraying him in upcoming movie
items.description: "It doesn't feel like it's in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life," Altman said.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Hollywood has found plenty of material and cinematic inspiration from a string of Silicon Valley scandals and power struggles in recent years. “ You Can See Everything ,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, smashed box office expectations, and Netflix’s limited series “The Altruists” comes out Thursday to tell the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the downfall of FTX. As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either. In “Artificial,” a biographical comedy-drama opening in theaters on Christmas, the lauded actor Andrew Garfield will portray Altman in a film that chronicles OpenAI’s rise and the internal turmoil that erupted when he was briefly ousted in 2023. “If you had told me 20 years ago that someone was going to make a movie about me, I think that would have struck me as … that would have been a very weird thing,” Altman said onstage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. “Now it doesn’t feel like it’s in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life.” Garfield is best known for his role as Spider-Man, but his big break came in 2010, when he played Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin in “The Social Network” alongside Jesse Eisenberg as Mark Zuckerberg. (That film also had a sequel of sorts this year called “ The Social Reckoning ,” but it bombed at the box office.)
